jp: 今日[きょう]はどうして早[はや]く帰[かえ]ってきた{んですか|pt-nda}。
en: Why did you come home early today?
why: A question asking for the reason behind a situation takes んですか; a bare verb cannot take ですか.

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]五時[ごじ]に起[お]きる{んです|pt-nda}。犬[いぬ]の散歩[さんぽ]をしなければなりませんから。
en: I get up at five every morning, you see. I have to walk the dog.
why: The speaker is explaining the background of a fact, which is what んです does.

jp: ごめん、今夜[こんや]は早[はや]く寝[ね]る{んだ|pt-nda}。明日[あした]は五時[ごじ]に起[お]きなきゃいけないから。
en: Sorry, I'm going to bed early tonight. I have to get up at five tomorrow.
why: The speaker is explaining why they are declining, so んだ; a bare verb cannot take だ.

jp: どうしてテレビを消[け]した{んですか|pt-nda}。まだ見[み]ていたのに。
en: Why did you turn off the TV? I was still watching it.
why: The speaker wants an explanation for what happened, so んですか; a bare past verb cannot take ですか.

jp: すみません、今日[きょう]は子[こ]どもを迎[むか]えに行[い]く{んです|pt-nda}。先[さき]に帰[かえ]ってもいいですか。
en: Excuse me, I have to pick up my child today. May I leave early?
why: Giving a reason that leads into a request is a typical use of んです.

jp: 床[ゆか]がぬれていますね。誰[だれ]が牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]をこぼした{んですか|pt-nda}。
en: The floor is wet. Who spilled the milk?
why: Asking about the cause of something visible takes んですか; a bare past verb cannot take ですか.

jp: 毎晩[まいばん]十二時[じゅうにじ]まで勉強[べんきょう]している{んです|pt-nda}。だから朝[あさ]はいつも眠[ねむ]いです。
en: I study until midnight every night, you see. That's why I'm always sleepy in the morning.
why: The sentence gives the explanation for what follows, so んです.
